```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) answers a question from your own
documents. It has two steps:

1. Retrieval: find the pieces of text most similar to the question.
2. Generation: give those pieces to a chat model with the question, and
   ask it to answer from them.

edgemodelr does both locally. The code in this vignette is not run when
the package is built, because it needs model files.

## Embeddings and similarity

An embedding is a numeric vector for a text. Texts with similar meaning
get vectors that point the same way. Load the model with
`embeddings = TRUE`:

```{r}
library(edgemodelr)

embedder <- edge_load_model("Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B-Q8_0.gguf", embeddings = TRUE)

e <- edge_embeddings(embedder, c(
  "cats purr when happy",
  "kittens purr",
  "the bond market fell"
))
dim(e)
#> [1]    3 1024
edge_model_n_embd(embedder)
#> [1] 1024
```

`edge_embeddings()` returns one row per text. By default each row is
scaled to length 1 (`normalize = TRUE`), so the dot product of two rows is
their cosine similarity.

`edge_similarity()` gives the cosine similarity of two vectors, from -1
to 1. `edge_similarity_matrix()` gives it for every pair of rows:

```{r}
edge_similarity(e[1, ], e[2, ])
#> [1] 0.7986
edge_similarity(e[1, ], e[3, ])
#> [1] 0.3275

round(edge_similarity_matrix(e), 3)
#>       [,1]  [,2]  [,3]
#> [1,] 1.000 0.799 0.328
#> [2,] 0.799 1.000 0.377
#> [3,] 0.328 0.377 1.000
```

Scores are only comparable between vectors from the same model.

## Choosing an embedding model

Use a model trained for embeddings. A chat model loaded with
`embeddings = TRUE` also gives vectors, but they separate topics less
well.

- Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B (Q8_0, about 600 MB) gives 1024 numbers per text
  and handles many languages. It is a good default.
- nomic-embed-text and similar models are smaller and faster, with
  768 numbers per text.

Embedding only reads text, so it is much faster than generating the
same number of tokens.

An embedding model cannot write answers. For the generation step, load a
chat model as well (see below).

## Building an index

`edge_index_documents()` splits documents into chunks, embeds each chunk
and returns an `edge_index` object. It takes either a character vector of
texts or a directory.

```{r}
docs <- c(
  "The library opens at 9am on weekdays and 10am on Saturdays. It is closed on Sundays.",
  "Members can borrow up to 12 books at a time for three weeks.",
  "Late returns cost 20 cents per book per day, up to 5 dollars.",
  "The reading room on the second floor has 40 desks and free wifi."
)
index <- edge_index_documents(docs, embedder)
index
#> edgemodelr RAG Index
#>   Chunks: 4
#>   Embedding dim: 1024
#>   Source: direct text input
```

For a directory, every file that matches `file_pattern` is read, also in
subfolders. The default pattern is `"*.txt"`:

```{r}
policy_index <- edge_index_documents("policies/", embedder, file_pattern = "*.md")
```

The index is a list with `chunks`, `embeddings` (one row per chunk),
`sources` (the file of each chunk, or `NA` for direct text), `n_chunks`
and `n_embd`.

## Chunking

Long texts are split into chunks of about `chunk_size` characters
(default 500), with `chunk_overlap` characters (default 50) repeated
between neighbouring chunks. A chunk ends at a sentence end when there is
one in its second half.

```{r}
policy_index <- edge_index_documents("policies/", embedder, file_pattern = "*.md",
                                     chunk_size = 300, chunk_overlap = 50)
```

Some guidance:

- A chunk should hold one idea, such as a paragraph or a rule. Chunks that
  are too long mix topics and match questions less well. Chunks that are
  too short lose their context.
- 300 to 800 characters suits most prose. Use smaller chunks for lists of
  short facts.
- The overlap keeps a sentence that falls on a boundary in at least one
  whole chunk. 10 to 20 percent of `chunk_size` is usually enough.
- A character vector is taken as chunks you made yourself. Only texts
  longer than twice `chunk_size` are split. This lets you chunk by your
  own rules, for example one chunk per row of a data frame.
- Each chunk must fit in the embedding model's context. `edge_tokenize()`
  counts tokens: `length(edge_tokenize(embedder, chunk))`.

## Searching

`edge_search()` embeds the query and returns the `top_k` most similar
chunks as a data frame:

```{r}
hits <- edge_search(index, embedder, "When is the library open on Saturday?",
                    top_k = 2)
hits
#>                                                                                  chunk     score source index
#> 1 The library opens at 9am on weekdays and 10am on Saturdays. It is closed on Sundays. 0.8356657   <NA>     1
#> 2                         Members can borrow up to 12 books at a time for three weeks. 0.4660888   <NA>     2
```

`score` is the cosine similarity, `source` the file and `index` the row in
the index. Use the same model for the query that built the index;
`edge_search()` stops with an error if the embedding sizes differ.

## Reranking

Embedding search is fast but rough. A reranking model reads the query and
each chunk together and scores how well the chunk answers it, which is
slower but more accurate. Give `edge_search()` a reranker and it rescores
the best `max(4 * top_k, 20)` embedding hits and returns the best `top_k`
in the reranker's order, with a `rerank_score` column:

```{r}
reranker <- edge_load_model("bge-reranker-v2-m3-Q4_K_M.gguf", reranking = TRUE)
edge_search(index, embedder, "When is the library open on Saturday?",
            top_k = 2, rerank = reranker)
```

`edge_rerank()` scores any documents against a query directly:

```{r}
edge_rerank(reranker, "What is the capital of France?",
            c("Paris is the capital of France.", "Berlin is in Germany."))
```

The scores are the model's raw scores, not probabilities, so compare them
only with each other.

## Answering with a separate chat model

With an embedding model for retrieval, load a chat model for the answer
and put the retrieved chunks in its system prompt:

```{r}
chat_model <- edge_load_model("gemma-3-1b-it-Q4_K_M.gguf", n_ctx = 4096)

ask <- function(question, top_k = 3) {
  hits <- edge_search(index, embedder, question, top_k = top_k)
  context <- paste0("[", seq_len(nrow(hits)), "] ", hits$chunk, collapse = "\n")
  edge_chat_completion(chat_model, list(
    list(role = "system", content = paste0(
      "Answer only from the context below. ",
      "If the answer is not there, say you do not know.\n\nContext:\n", context)),
    list(role = "user", content = question)
  ), n_predict = 200, temperature = 0)
}

ask("How much is the late fee per day?")
ask("Is there parking?")
```

`edge_chat_completion()` uses the chat model's own template, which most
models need to follow instructions well.

## Answering with edge_ask()

`edge_ask()` does retrieval and generation in one call. `ctx` embeds the
question, so it must be the model that built the index. By default the
same `ctx` also writes the answer; with an embedding-only model, pass a
chat model as `chat_ctx`:

```{r}
edge_ask(embedder, "How much is the late fee per day?", index, top_k = 2,
         chat_ctx = chat_model)
```

A chat model loaded with `embeddings = TRUE` can do both:

```{r}
ctx <- edge_load_model("gemma-3-1b-it-Q4_K_M.gguf", embeddings = TRUE)
ctx_index <- edge_index_documents(docs, ctx)

edge_ask(ctx, "How much is the late fee per day?", ctx_index, top_k = 2)
```

With `return_context = TRUE` it returns a list with `answer`, `context`
(the `edge_search()` result) and `prompt`, which helps you see why an
answer is wrong:

```{r}
res <- edge_ask(ctx, "How much is the late fee per day?", ctx_index,
                top_k = 2, return_context = TRUE)
res$context$score
cat(res$prompt)
```

`edge_ask()` writes a plain prompt with `### Context` and `### Question`
sections rather than the model's chat template. Answers can run on past
the answer. Set `n_predict` low, or use the two-model pattern above.

## Saving and reusing an index

An index is an ordinary R object. Save it with `saveRDS()` and load it in
a later session, so the documents are embedded only once:

```{r}
saveRDS(index, "library-index.rds")

# Later
index <- readRDS("library-index.rds")
embedder <- edge_load_model("Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B-Q8_0.gguf", embeddings = TRUE)
edge_search(index, embedder, "How many books can I borrow?", top_k = 1)
```

The model context itself cannot be saved. Load the same embedding model
again before you search. If you change the model or the chunking, build
the index again.

To add documents, index only the new ones and combine the parts:

```{r}
new <- edge_index_documents(c("Parking is free for members after 6pm."), embedder)

index$chunks <- c(index$chunks, new$chunks)
index$embeddings <- rbind(index$embeddings, new$embeddings)
index$sources <- c(index$sources, new$sources)
index$n_chunks <- length(index$chunks)
```

## Cleaning up

```{r}
edge_free_model(embedder)
edge_free_model(chat_model)
edge_free_model(reranker)
edge_free_model(ctx)
```

For a larger document store with search by keywords as well as meaning,
see the ragnar package. `embed_edge()` lets ragnar embed locally; see
`vignette("ellmer", package = "edgemodelr")`.
